You're absolutely right—I had that backwards. My apologies!

- **localStorage**: Shared across all tabs/windows of the same origin; persists after browser close
- **sessionStorage**: Scoped per tab/window; cleared when the tab closes
- **Cookies**: Also shared across tabs of the same origin

So if you're storing a login flag in localStorage, it would absolutely be visible and accessible from a second tab on the same origin. That could definitely explain why users are getting automatically logged in on a second tab—the flag is there for all tabs to read.

If you want to prevent cross-tab login behavior, you could either:
1. Use `sessionStorage` instead (keeps it isolated to a single tab)
2. Keep using localStorage but add logic to detect and handle cross-tab login scenarios (like validating the session server-side)
3. Listen to `storage` events to be notified when localStorage changes in other tabs and handle it accordingly

What's the intended behavior you're trying to achieve?
